name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean in a heavily Republican northwest Georgia seat
Incumbent Clay Fuller running for reelection with strong outside support ($2.8M)
Prediction markets price Fuller at 94% to win
Harris outraised Fuller heavily but spent it all, with little cash left
model.rationale: The R+19 district and an incumbent Republican make this a Safe R race, and markets agree at 94% for Fuller. Harris's large fundraising total is notable but was spent down to almost nothing, and outside money overwhelmingly backs Fuller, so the fundamentals-based margin near R+17 stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Harris within single digits, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would warrant moving this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Georgia's 14th District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+19. Incumbent Clay Fuller returns after easily securing his party's nomination and faces Democrat Shawn Harris and a minor Libertarian candidate in the general election. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on the district's fundamentals and market pricing.

Harris raised far more money than Fuller, about $8.1 million, but reports almost no cash on hand, while outside groups have spent heavily supporting Fuller and attacking Harris. Prediction markets give Fuller roughly a 94% chance of winning. The forecast expects Fuller to win by a wide, double-digit margin, with low but nonzero uncertainty given the absence of polling.
